claim: At 5-step checkpoint spacing, seeds 56, 57, 58, 62 and 63 (N=64, e<=0.5) first hold the accel_step margin at or above 0.1 for good at steps 80, 85, 90, 100 and 95. That is the same 80-100 window seen at 10-step spacing, so checkpoint resolution does not explain it. Half-final steps, read from the trajectories, are 70, 65, 70, 60 and 85, and only 3 of 5 seeds (56, 57, 58) meet both expected-if-true ranges. Final accel_step R2 is 0.875-0.909 against controls of 0.709-0.769 (margins 0.139-0.173). Force never beats its control: final margins are 0.051-0.080, after an early transient of 0.15-0.17 at steps 10-15 that falls to about 0 by step 40.
confidence_note: Neither preset outcome happened. Expected-if-true needed 4 of 5 seeds in range on both measures, but only 3 of 5 qualified: seed 62's persistent step is 100 and seed 63's half-final step is 85. Expected-if-false needed 3 of 5 seeds out of range, but only those same 2 were. The other conditions held: all 5 runs completed 300/300 steps, every final margin is at least 0.1, and val_mse_ratio is 0.66-0.70 at step 200, first dropping below 1 at steps 140-160. The data do go against the stated hypothesis. Persistent formation at 80-100 matches the earlier 10-step reads for these seeds (56-58 were 80/90/90 at 10-step spacing). Seeds 65-69 (65-90) sit only about 10-15 steps earlier, which is inside the seed-to-seed spread. So the earlier window looks like ordinary seed variation, not a resolution artifact. The 0.1-bar step is fragile when a run levels off near the threshold: seed 62 stays at a margin of 0.095-0.097 from step 80 to 95 and crosses only at 100. The two timing measures also order seeds differently (seed 62 has the earliest half-final step and the latest persistent step). In all 5 runs formed_at_step equals the trajectory crossing, with no one-checkpoint lag. Per-seed control R2 does not order the persistent steps (seed 57 has the highest control, 0.769, but forms at 85). What would change the verdict: a pre-registered single criterion, or more 5-step seeds, showing the 65-90 and 80-100 groups differ by more than their within-group spread.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 2): Accepted. The pre-registered criteria were not met either way (3 of 5 seeds in range against the 4 of 5 needed, and 2 of 5 out of range against the 3 of 5 needed). So the finding can only say that at 5-step spacing these seeds form persistently at 80/85/90/100/95 and reach half-final at 70/65/70/60/85, close to their 10-step reads. 'Checkpoint resolution does not explain it' and 'looks like ordinary seed variation' are interpretations the experiment did not decide. They should be read as hypotheses, not conclusions. The status stays inconclusive.
